triggers: active model or tool policy changes materially
a host version or source revision changes
an upstream dependency or source version changes
a regression or contradiction is observed

modalities.contract: One model-qualified user-owned instruction profile binds exact host artifacts and context budgets; provider/runtime-native layers remain identified external owners and project-local instructions retain native precedence.

hermes.owner: recovery/current/hosts/hermes/SOUL.md plus Hermes native prompt builder
hermes.mechanism: restore the hash-bound user-global SOUL overlay; keep runtime-native system assembly and project context external/native

codex.mechanism: restore the hash-bound global AGENTS overlay while preserving project and tree-scoped overrides

omp.owner: Codex AGENTS inheritance plus OMP native prompt builder
omp.mechanism: inherit the hash-bound current Codex global overlay; the duplicate OMP RULES delta is retired

intentional_deltas: Codex keeps hierarchical repository instruction scoping.
Hermes keeps personality selection and frozen per-session prompt behavior.
OMP inherits the Codex global overlay instead of maintaining a duplicate RULES file.
Provider-hidden and runtime-native system instructions are version-qualified external dependencies, not copied artifacts.

modalities.contract: Portable procedures use the Agent Skills directory format from one canonical tree; each host retains native discovery, triggering, and lifecycle UX.

hermes.mechanism: register the canonical skills directory as an external source

codex.mechanism: link admitted skill directories individually into the standard user scope

omp.mechanism: use thin discovery adapters that load the canonical portable owner when OMP does not enumerate Windows directory junctions

intentional_deltas: Hermes retains hub install, explicit preload, and curator lifecycle features.
Codex retains its native discovery scopes and plugin-bundled skills.
OMP uses a thin real-directory discovery adapter for the canonical outcome-first owner because its /skills enumeration omitted the Windows junction; direct invocation succeeded.

modalities.contract: Tool intent and acceptance tests are portable; MCP is preferred for shared external tools, while high-value host-native tools remain native.

hermes.mechanism: map shared tools to MCP or plugins; retain service-gated core tools

codex.mechanism: map shared tools to MCP; retain Codex-native execution and app-server tools

omp.owner: built-in tools, extensions, and MCP configuration
omp.mechanism: map shared tools to MCP or extensions while retaining OMP-native execution and IDE tooling

intentional_deltas: Core tool schemas and approval UX are host-owned and need not be identical.

modalities.contract: Observable task-class reliability, p95 latency, total expected cost, and failure cost determine speed- or intelligence-constrained routes; release research is portable while provider names, model IDs, effort controls, and orchestration primitives remain host-native.

hermes.owner: routed-delegation plugin plus native child builder/finalizer
hermes.mechanism: the live user plugin selects and pins exact per-child routes through a version-guarded native seam; routed_workflow consumes the definitive portable DAG state owner and adds trusted manifest and close-witness bindings; catalogue refresh remains manual and built-in delegate_task remains the homogeneous rollback path

codex.owner: skills/dynamic-workflows state contract plus native worker handles
codex.mechanism: initialize one exact selector receipt per DAG node, pass model and reasoning effort directly to the native worker, verify the effective route, and close the handle before terminal state

omp.owner: skills/dynamic-workflows state contract plus exact route named agents
omp.mechanism: initialize the same receipt, dispatch route-<route-id> agents that pin exact openai-codex model and thinkingLevel, and reject resolved-model fallback

intentional_deltas: Hosts may expose different subagent, fallback, and reasoning controls.
Catalogue refresh is manual; no host polls releases or Artificial Analysis at runtime.
A fixed weak route is never used for substantive judgment merely to force mechanism parity.
Workflow retries reuse one receipt; failed tasks do not climb the reasoning-effort ladder automatically.

modalities.contract: Agents query prior context on demand from its authoritative source, return a small provenance-scoped result, and share only admitted durable facts, preferences, and decisions without copying transcript bodies or duplicating repository, skill, or task-system authority.

hermes.owner: session_search, compact built-in memory, skills, authoritative artifacts, and the native session store
hermes.mechanism: query the authoritative source on demand; keep external providers and broad automatic memory injection disabled unless a concrete repeated miss passes a bounded admission trial

codex.mechanism: keep thread state native and defer a shared provider until one passes the cross-host admission suite

omp.owner: native memory backend and session persistence
omp.mechanism: keep memory.backend off; defer local, Hindsight, or Mnemopi activation until a canonical shared provider is admitted

intentional_deltas: Raw memories, user profiles, and transcripts remain private and host-local.
Hermes retired Honcho and Hindsight after the later real-history utility audit found no repeatable external-only downstream win; this is not a claim that external memory can never help.

Codex and OMP remain unintegrated because Hindsight 0.9.1 failed candidate-only irrelevant-query silence, tool-visible provenance, and Windows lifecycle checks through the real Hermes recall path; no matched provider comparison ran.

modalities.contract: Shared safety outcomes are tested across hosts; sandbox, approvals, hooks, redaction, and policy enforcement use each host's native mechanisms.

hermes.owner: approvals, hooks, safe mode, redaction, and allowlists
hermes.mechanism: thin Hermes policy adapter only where instructions cannot enforce the contract

codex.owner: sandbox, approval policy, exec policy, and managed hooks
codex.mechanism: thin Codex policy adapter only where instructions cannot enforce the contract

omp.owner: approval modes, hooks, tool controls, and configuration
omp.mechanism: use OMP-native approval and extension boundaries; add adapters only for portable checks

intentional_deltas: Hook schemas, trust models, and sandbox guarantees remain host-specific.

modalities.contract: Plans express outcomes, dependencies, and acceptance checks portably; durable execution maps to each host's native task, background, scheduling, or external automation mechanism.

hermes.owner: todo, background work, cron, goals, and worktrees
hermes.mechanism: map portable plan intent to the smallest native durable primitive

codex.owner: plans, non-interactive exec, collaboration modes, and external automation
codex.mechanism: map portable plan intent to Codex plan/exec or an external scheduler

omp.owner: todo, task agents, sessions, extensions, and external automation
omp.mechanism: map portable plan intent to OMP todo/task agents or an external scheduler

intentional_deltas: Hermes cron and gateway delivery need not be emulated inside Codex.
Codex-native plan streaming need not be emulated inside Hermes.

modalities.contract: Admission, installation, drift detection, reevaluation, rollback, and pruning are reproducible while host self-update and marketplace lifecycle remain native.

hermes.owner: doctor, update, config migration, skills lifecycle, and curator
hermes.mechanism: use repository evidence for admission and Hermes curator for post-admission lifecycle

codex.owner: installer, config reload, plugin lifecycle, and skill refresh
codex.mechanism: use repository evidence for admission and Codex-native refresh/update behavior

omp.owner: plugin lifecycle, update command, rules, and skill discovery
omp.mechanism: use repository evidence for admission and OMP-native plugin/update behavior

intentional_deltas: Host installers, release channels, and lifecycle UIs remain native.
